props.title: Haunted Mansion

sections.content: Disney's second attempt at adapting their iconic theme park attraction improves on **The Haunted Mansion (2023)** (2003) with Eddie Murphy, but still struggles to capture the ride's perfect blend of spooky fun and gothic atmosphere. **Haunted Mansion** (2023) follows LaKeith Stanfield as a grieving astrophysicist-turned-ghost-tour-guide who gets wrapped up in supernatural happenings alongside a single mom (Rosario Dawson) and her son. The film draws clear inspiration from family-friendly horror classics like **The Monster Squad** (1987) and **Casper** (1995), aiming to balance genuine scares with lighthearted comedy.

sections.content: Director Justin Simien brings some stylish visual flair but can't quite nail the tonal balance that made **The Addams Family** (1991) and **Beetlejuice** (1988) such enduring hits. The impressive ensemble cast including Owen Wilson, Danny DeVito, and Jamie Lee Curtis feels underutilized, though Jared Leto's take on the Hatbox Ghost provides some memorably creepy moments. The film's strongest elements come from directly adapting iconic ride moments like the stretching portraits and the ghostly ballroom sequence.

The movie fits into Disney's recent trend of mining their theme park attractions for film potential, following **Jungle Cruise** (2021) and **Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl** (2003). While it doesn't reach the heights of the first Pirates film, it demonstrates more understanding of its source material than misfire adaptations like **Tomorrowland** (2015). movies.title: House
movies.slug: This psychedelic Japanese horror-comedy follows seven schoolgirls visiting a very strange house with a hunger for young souls

sections.content: Theme park rides-turned-movies face unique storytelling hurdles, needing to expand 10-minute experiences into feature-length narratives while retaining their essence. **Mission: Impossible** (1996) successfully reinvented its source TV show, while **The Country Bears** (2002) and **Tower of Terror** (1997) struggled to justify their existence beyond brand recognition. **Haunted Mansion** (2023) falls somewhere in between, offering enough fan service to please Disney parks enthusiasts while sometimes getting bogged down in unnecessary mythology.
